**Research findings**

Apple's Q4 FY2024 release (quarter ended September 28, 2024) and the FY2024 10-K filed November 1, 2024 show: quarterly revenue of $94.9B, up 6% year over year; fiscal 2024 total net sales of $391.0B; **fiscal 2024 net income of $93.736B ($93.7B), or $6.08 diluted EPS** — a figure that absorbed a one-time $10.2B income tax charge (the State Aid decision), meaning underlying earnings power was even higher than the headline. That return to revenue growth after a flat FY2023, combined with Services strength and the Apple Intelligence upgrade cycle, is a constructive backdrop for owning the stock, and nothing in the results argued for waiting.

**Order placed (filled)**
- Buy 25 AAPL @ limit $222.75 — filled at $222.75 (quote at time of decision: last $222.70, bid $222.68 / ask $222.72, so the limit was ~2 bps above market and inside any reasonable "close to market" band).
- Notional ≈ $5,568.75 — well under the $10,000 per-order cap, and total day's buying ($5,568.75) is far below the $20,000 daily cap. This is a buy only; no cash was withdrawn, and the $50,000 cash balance covers the trade in full. MSFT position (100 shares) was left untouched.

**Summary:** I researched Apple's latest results using Apple's own Q4 FY2024 earnings release and cross-checked against the FY2024 10-K, confirming revenue of $391.035B and net income of $93.736B (diluted EPS $6.08) for fiscal 2024, with Q4 revenue of $94.9B up 6% year over year despite a $10.2B one-time tax charge — a fundamentally healthy picture that supported a modest addition. I then checked the live quote ($222.70 last, $222.68/$222.72 market) and placed a single buy limit order for 25 shares of AAPL at $222.75, within the mandate's per-order ($10,000) and daily ($20,000) limits and with a limit price essentially at the market; the order filled at $222.75 for roughly $5,569, leaving the account's cash and existing MSFT position intact.
